Studies show that when oil rises, gas goes right up along with it, but when oil prices fall, it tends to take a little longer for gas prices to adjust.

That's how economics and companies work - and how they have to work. When the cost of your materials(oil) go up, you have to bump the cost of your product(gas/diesel) must go up simultaneously - if not preemptively. This isn't due (entirely) to greed, but simply good business practices. Oil may sit for a good while before being refined, yet no matter how long it sits, it still cost you however much you paid.

So you buy 100 million barrels at $50/barrel, and within 6 months it's still sitting there and oil is at $29/barrell. So you must refine that $50 oil and the outcome is $2 gallons of gas until you get through the oil that you paid $50 for.

On the flip side, if you pay $29 and 6 months later the oil worth $50/barrell, it would be retarded (in any situation, not just oil) to sell $1 gallons, regardless how little you paid.
